p1: The Lord showed Isaiah things far in the future. Isaiah told about a book that was sealed, closed up tight.
Someone asked a wise man to read it. He said, “I cannot; for it is sealed.”
Some people praised the Lord with words, but not with their hearts. So the Lord said, “I will do a marvelous work and a wonder.” It would be something amazing!
p2: Prophets in our day teach that Isaiah was talking about the Book of Mormon. It is a book about Jesus. Even people who could not hear would “hear the words of the book.”
You can hear those words too. Tonight, touch a Book of Mormon if you can. Its words help you know Jesus.
old: This week’s book is named after something Isaiah said Heavenly Father would do: “a marvellous work and a wonder!”
That means Heavenly Father does amazing, surprising, wonderful things — things so good and clever that they make us say, “Wow!”
Isaiah promised that Heavenly Father would do a wonder that would help all His children — teaching and blessing even those who thought they couldn’t learn.
Heavenly Father is full of surprises! He can make wonderful things happen in ways we never even imagined. His works are truly marvelous.
When you see something amazing — a rainbow, a new baby, a kind miracle — you can remember: Heavenly Father is still doing marvelous works and wonders, today and always.
